### 💡 Codex Review Here are some automated review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `78df81a786`
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
Codex has been enabled to automatically review pull requests in this repo. Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. When you [sign up for Codex through ChatGPT](https://openai.com/codex), Codex can also answer questions or update the PR, like "@codex address that feedback".

Hey @pcbeingused333, thank you for your contribution!

The crash is real and the parser is the right place to fix it. Two changes are needed before this can merge:

1. **Row value.** With this patch the RESP3 row becomes `[]`, but the RESP2 parser (`_get_aggregate_result`) passes the server null through, so the same reply gives `None` there. The two protocols must return the same shape, most strictly with `legacy_responses=False`. Please keep the null row as `None` on RESP3 too, and keep `[]` only for the case where the `extra_attributes` key is missing.
2. **Test location.** The parser tests live in `tests/test_search_result.py`, next to `test_bytes_keys_are_parsed`. Please move the test there, call `_parse_aggregate_resp3` directly through the `_make_search()` helper, and drop the function-level imports. `tests/test_search_aggregation.py` is for request building.

Could you also reply to and resolve the two Codex threads? The import one goes away with the move. The asyncio one is not needed, since both stacks share this one parser function.

Small note: the description says `protocol=3, legacy_responses=False`, but the default client (RESP3 wire with legacy shapes) and `FT.PROFILE` on an aggregate request hit the same path. Please update it.

The shared parser also serves `AsyncSearchCommands.aggregate`, but this regression constructs only the synchronous client. Root `AGENTS.md` explicitly requires testing both stacks, so add an async `fixed_client` counterpart using `redis.asyncio.Redis` and an `AsyncMock` response, asserting that the live row is preserved and the expired row becomes empty. The implementation is already shared; the missing piece is coverage through the async entry point.
